newsitem.title: USA: Kodak moves advertising to Ogilvy & Mather.
newsitem.headline: Kodak moves advertising to Ogilvy & Mather.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. said Monday it is assigning all advertising for its consumer imaging business to Ogilvy & Mather Worldwide, dropping its long-time ad agency J. Walter Thompson Co.
Starting July 1, Ogilvy will handle advertising for Kodak film and traditional cameras, which was previously handled by J. Walter Thompson, Kodak said.
Billings were not disclosed, but industry sources put the figure in the $40 million to $50 million range worldwide.
J. Walter Thompson and Ogilvy & Mather are both units of WPP Group Plc.
"This switch in advertising assignments for Kodak consumer products reflects our need for a new creative focus and direction," said Carl Gustin, Kodak's chief marketing officer, in a statement.

J. Walter Thompson's relationship with Kodak spanned more than six decades. Chris Jones, CEO of J. Walter Thompson Worldwide in New York, said the company was disappointed but not surprised by the decision.

"When a company undergoes the level of change that Kodak is going through, any long-serving partner is vulnerable," he said in a statement. "We leave this relationship with enormous pride in what we have accomplished to help build this wonderful brand, right up to our most recent work."
Ogilvy already handled Advantix Advanced Photo System products, one-time-use cameras, and corporate brand advertising, Kodak said.

A Kodak spokesman cited the need for a "new creative approach" to advertising in explaining the shift in agencies and said Kodak had been pleased with Ogilvy's performance on the accounts it has handled since last year.
